bug_description.normalized: When the staged font is shaped against the harness's fixed UTF-8 witness string, HarfBuzz reaches end-of-text inside AAT `morx` ligature processing. An attacker-controlled `CLASS_END_OF_TEXT` ligature entry records the current output position in `match_positions`, and a later `PerformAction` pop passes that recorded output index into `hb_buffer_t::move_to()`. On the crashing path the popped value equals the current output-end position, so `move_to()` leaves `buffer->idx == buffer->len`. The vulnerable code then evaluates `buffer->cur().codepoint + offset` without first checking `idx < len`, so `cur()` reads `info[len].codepoint` from spare heap storage that `hb_buffer_t::enlarge()` allocated but the UTF-8 load never initialized. That uninitialized codepoint becomes `component_idx`, is used to select `component[component_idx]`, and MemorySanitizer reports the resulting use of uninitialized data in `hb_sanitize_context_t::check_range`.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSAN origin. `realloc` enlarges the glyph-info array for the harness's fixed UTF-8 buffer but does not initialize the newly added spare `hb_glyph_info_t` slots.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved MSAN trace attributes the uninitialized value to this heap allocation and shows it was reached from `hb_buffer_add_utf<hb_utf8_t>` during the first fixed-string shaping block at `test/fuzzing/hb-shape-fuzzer.cc:18`.

source.description: First project statement on the vulnerability-causing end-of-text path that materializes attacker-controlled `morx` state. Once the driver reaches `CLASS_END_OF_TEXT`, this lookup fetches the ligature entry whose flags and action index drive the later unsafe transition.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is an sfnt font blob whose directory includes a `morx` table. When shaping the harness's fixed UTF-8 string reaches `buffer->idx == buffer->len`, line 561 reads the corresponding `CLASS_END_OF_TEXT` ligature entry from that attacker-controlled table.
source.note: This is the scored source rather than the fuzzer entry point because it is the first project-side statement that turns the staged font bytes into the specific entry/flags consumed by the vulnerable ligature logic.

root_cause.description: Missing end-of-text guard. After `move_to()` the ligature action loop still reads the current glyph and computes `component_idx` even when the cursor remains at `idx == len`.
root_cause.note: The fix for issue 10990 inserts `if (buffer->idx >= buffer->len) return false;` immediately before this line, preventing the end-of-text `cur()` read.

sink.code: bool ok = this->max_ops-- > 0 && this->start <= p && p <= this->end && (unsigned int) (this->end - p) >= len;
sink.description: MSAN crash site. `check_range` consumes pointer `p` derived from `component[component_idx]`, and `component_idx` carries the uninitialized `info[len].codepoint` read on the vulnerable end-of-text path.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `src/hb-machinery.hh:286:25` with frames through `OT::IntType<unsigned short, 2u>::sanitize` and `AAT::LigatureSubtable::driver_context_t::transition`.

parser_admitted.note: The staged font reaches the AAT substitution path because `_get_morx` returns a non-empty `morx` table. The staged `poc` hexdump shows the `morx` tag in the font directory.

fixed_text_buffer.note: The MSAN origin stack ties the uninitialized glyph-info allocation to the first fixed-string shaping block, so the witnessed crash occurs while shaping `ABCDEXYZ123@_%&)*$!`.

coarse_trace.summary: Growing the glyph-info array for the harness's fixed UTF-8 buffer leaves spare heap slots uninitialized beyond the logical glyph run.

When the driver reaches end-of-text, it fetches attacker-controlled `CLASS_END_OF_TEXT` ligature entries from the font's `morx` table; one such end-of-text path records the current output position into `match_positions` for later ligature action processing.

A later `PerformAction` transition pops that recorded output index, `move_to()` leaves the cursor at end-of-text, and the code computes `buffer->cur().codepoint + offset` without checking `idx < len`, reading `info[len]`.
Sanitization of `component[component_idx]` reaches `check_range`, where the pointer derived from the uninitialized `component_idx` triggers the observed MSAN report.

fine_trace.note: MSAN origin: `realloc` grows `buffer->info` for the fixed UTF-8 shaping run. The new tail capacity is not initialized, so spare `hb_glyph_info_t` slots beyond the live glyph sequence contain indeterminate heap bytes.

`hb_buffer_add_utf8()` appends one real glyph at a time through `add()`. This zeroes only the current `info[len]` slot before `len++`, so after the last real glyph the first unused slot `info[len]` is still the uninitialized spare capacity from step 1.

After earlier loop iterations consume the live glyphs, `buffer->idx == buffer->len`, so the ternary takes the `CLASS_END_OF_TEXT` arm and `get_entryZ` fetches the corresponding ligature entry from the attacker-controlled `morx` table.

`match_positions` elements are produced from `buffer->out_len` at this `SetComponent` site. The only other writer is line 421, which runs only after the vulnerable read at line 409, so the pre-read element later popped at line 399 must come from an execution of line 385. On the end-of-text ligature path it records the output cursor at the logical end position.
The ligature action loop pops the top recorded output position and passes it to `move_to()` as output-buffer index `i` before reading the current glyph.

`LigatureSubtable::driver_context_t` runs with `in_place = false`, so `drive()` has already enabled output mode and `move_to()` takes its output-buffer path. On the end-of-text call site `len - idx` is 0, so line 384 requires `i <= out_len`; if `i < out_len`, lines 395-408 would rewind `idx` below `len`. The crashing path therefore has `i == out_len`, leaving `idx == len` for the next `cur()` read.

From the attacker-controlled ligature entry, `action_idx` selects a ligature action word. The code sanitizes `ligAction[action_idx]` and sign-extends its 30-bit offset field into the signed `offset` used in the next arithmetic step.

fine_trace.code: inline hb_glyph_info_t &cur (unsigned int i = 0) { return info[idx + i]; }
fine_trace.note: `cur()` aliases `info[idx]`. With step 6 leaving `idx == len`, this resolves to `info[len]`, the first unused glyph-info slot past the initialized run from step 2, so the `codepoint` field is still the uninitialized heap data from step 1.

Root cause. The code computes `component_idx` from `buffer->cur().codepoint + offset` without checking `buffer->idx < buffer->len` after `move_to()`. On this end-of-text path the left operand comes from the uninitialized `info[len].codepoint` exposed in step 8.

fine_trace.code:
const HBUINT16 &componentData = component[component_idx];
if (unlikely (!componentData.sanitize (&c->sanitizer))) return false;
fine_trace.note: The uninitialized-derived `component_idx` indexes the attacker-controlled component table and immediately feeds the resulting `componentData` into OpenType sanitization.

fine_trace.code:
bool ok = this->max_ops-- > 0 &&
          this->start <= p &&
          p <= this->end &&
          (unsigned int) (this->end - p) >= len;
fine_trace.note: Sink. `componentData.sanitize()` reaches `check_struct()` / `check_range()`, where pointer `p` derived from `component[component_idx]` is compared against the table bounds. MSAN reports the uninitialized value here at `src/hb-machinery.hh:286:25`.

patch_analysis.patch_description: The fix adds a single end-of-text guard inside `AAT::LigatureSubtable::driver_context_t::transition`: `if (buffer->idx >= buffer->len) return false;` immediately before `buffer->cur().codepoint + offset`.

key_changes.change: Inserted `if (buffer->idx >= buffer->len) return false;` before `unsigned int component_idx = buffer->cur().codepoint + offset;`, blocking the end-of-text `cur()` read.

allocation_stack.function: void hb_buffer_add_utf<hb_utf8_t>(hb_buffer_t*, hb_utf8_t::codepoint_t const*, int, unsigned int, int)

poc.trigger: Supplying the staged `poc` font to `hb-shape-fuzzer` makes AAT `morx` ligature processing reach end-of-text while shaping the harness's fixed string `ABCDEXYZ123@_%&)*$!`; the ligature path records and later reuses the output-end position, then reads `buffer->cur().codepoint` with `idx == len`, which MSAN reports in `hb_sanitize_context_t::check_range`.

format.name: sfnt font with morx ligature table
format.contract: The staged witness is a compact sfnt font whose directory includes `morx` and whose AAT ligature state machine reaches end-of-text while shaping the fixed UTF-8 string `ABCDEXYZ123@_%&)*$!`, so the output-end position is reused as the current position before `buffer->cur().codepoint + offset`. No broader class beyond this witnessed end-of-text ligature corner case is claimed.
